textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · A Journey through States of Water · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Water from puddles, wet clothes and ponds goes into the air as an invisible gas called water vapour. This change is evaporation.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Water from puddles, wet clothes and ponds goes into the air as an invisible gas called water vapour. This change is evaporation. The reverse also happens: water vapour cooling to form drops is condensation.
beats.speakEn: Water from puddles, wet clothes and ponds goes into the air as an invisible gas called water vapour. This change is evaporation. The reverse also happens: water vapour cooling to form drops is condensation.

beats.en: Water exists in three states: solid ice, liquid water and gaseous water vapour. Ice melts into water when heated. This is melting. Water freezes into ice when cooled. This is freezing.
beats.speakEn: Water exists in three states: solid ice, liquid water and gaseous water vapour. Ice melts into water when heated. This is melting. Water freezes into ice when cooled. This is freezing.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · A Journey through States of Water · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Evaporation is faster when it is hot, when there is wind, when the surface is wide and when the air is dry. That is why clothes dry faster in the sun and on a windy day.

beats.en: Evaporation is faster when it is hot, when there is wind, when the surface is wide and when the air is dry. That is why clothes dry faster in the sun and on a windy day.
beats.speakEn: Evaporation is faster when it is hot, when there is wind, when the surface is wide and when the air is dry. That is why clothes dry faster in the sun and on a windy day.

beats.en: Evaporation takes heat from the surroundings, so it cools. Sweat evaporating cools our skin, and water in a clay pot cools because of evaporation from the pot's surface.
beats.speakEn: Evaporation takes heat from the surroundings, so it cools. Sweat evaporating cools our skin, and water in a clay pot cools because of evaporation from the pot's surface.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · A Journey through States of Water · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: The Sun heats seas and lakes. Water evaporates, rises and cools to form tiny drops that make clouds. When the drops grow heavy, they fall as rain. This is part of the water cycle.
